findings.issue: A path-named JSON value (path/file/paths/dir/cwd/… or an element of such an array) that holds MORE THAN ONE path — space- or comma-separated — is judged as ONE path. When the value's first segment is relative (so containment reads the whole string as an in-project relative path) but a later piece is an out-of-project absolute, POSIX-root, home (~), env ($HOME), Windows drive-relative or PowerShell-provider path, neither containment, nor the host (it joins the whole nonsense string and Evaluates it to Allow), nor the name screen (the embedded path spells no rule literal and no recorded withheld name) catches it, and the summary is shown verbatim. This is exactly the out-of-project path disclosure D50/D63 exist to prevent. Path-named values are exempt from the free-text whitelist (D63(1)), so nothing else screens them. D63 §23 item 6's completeness assumes 'a path-named value is one path' ("Read/Write/Edit take an absolute file_path, so a rooted plain path is judged as the one file it names"); a value that is a path LIST or a relative path followed by whitespace+absolute breaks that assumption. Not one of the three known-being-fixed w19h items.
findings.fix: In pathNamedWithheld (and the containment-only multi-value branch, and cutValueWithheld), stop treating the value as a single path when it contains interior whitespace or a comma: split the value on whitespace and commas and run the existing per-piece outside check (readingsOutside/startsOutside/hasDotDot, as free text already does with tokenOutside) over each piece, withholding if any piece names an absolute/home/drive/provider/escaping path — in addition to the whole-value containment+host judgement. A single legitimate in-project path with a space (src/my notes.txt) still passes (no piece starts outside). Add a red-first row with these 8 shapes to summary_privacy_test.go and the daemon twin.

findings.issue: Hosted `test (macos-latest)` will almost certainly fail tonight. On macOS, shortProjectDir builds the root from os.MkdirTemp("", "q") with no shortening; it canonicalises only on Windows. The macos-latest TMPDIR is 48 characters plus its trailing '/'. The fixture command `docker run -v "<root>:/src" -w /src img go test ./...` with root <TMPDIR>q<digits>/John Smith/proj is 113+d characters, where d is MkdirTemp's random suffix length. For d>=8 (about 99.8% of uniform uint32 suffixes) that exceeds the store's 120-character preview width, so storePreview's require.NotContains("…") fails before Build runs. EXPECTED_FAILING_ROWS and EXPECTED_FAILING_PACKAGES are empty, so the job goes red. No test of candidate 8 has ever run on macOS: the w19 reports say 'macOS is still unrun (GOOS=darwin vet only)'.

findings.location: internal/rehydrate/pathgate.go:283 (newPathJudge drop loop) and pathgate.go:2549 (gateCheckpointDrops); cost doc at internal/daemon/rehydrate_service.go:762-769 and ADR 0011 §23 item 10
findings.issue: Performance regression since candidate 7 (introduced by 00f324f1/7f90567f). Every path-keyed checkpoint drop entry (file_pointer, pointer_missing, pointer_invalid, pointer_untracked, pointer_dirty) now costs one host judgement through RuleSet.Evaluate, which takes about 1 ms on Windows and is not cached, and two Evaluates when the root resolves elsewhere. The number of drops has no bound. Draft.upsertFilePointerLocked (checkpoint/writer.go:1237) collects every distinct captured file, and Truncate cuts down to the 12K-token checkpoint budget with one file_pointer drop per pointer it cuts, so a large session hands Build hundreds or thousands of such drops. Build time then grows linearly with the drop count and approaches the 5 s compactAnswerBudget. Past that budget the model gets the deferred note instead of the rehydration. At a357d187 the build cost stayed flat at any drop count. No test covers the scaling: the cost rows carry no drops, and the doc's 'at most two Evaluates for each of those' gives no overall bound.
findings.evidence: Scratch copy of 2bf29705, internal/daemon overlay test TestZZRehyDrops through the real adapter (rehydrateHostPaths + mcpOpHostPolicy) on a realistic checkpoint (20 file pointers, 60 tool pointers), adding N file_pointer drops `pkg/subK/fileN.go`. Command: `go test -p 1 -count=1 -run '^TestZZRehyDrops$' -v ./internal/daemon/`. Through an NTFS junction root (TestZZRehyJunction, the adapter's second Evaluate on the resolved spelling): n=1000 p50 2.851s max 3.144s, against 1.743s on the canonical root. Per-call RuleSet.Evaluate cost: p50 1.07ms, p99 2.19ms, including a repeated existing path.

findings.evidence: I wrote a scratch benchmark, BenchmarkZZAuditBuild (perf/zz_audit_rehydrate_bench_test.go), and built it into both trees' internal/daemon. Fixture: 200 tool pointers in 8 store-preview shapes (Read/Edit file_path, Bash, Grep, Glob, Task JSON, root-led cd+rg), 50 file pointers, and the real rehydrateHostPaths over hostperm.New. I ran 6 interleaved rounds per variant with GOMAXPROCS=4 and compared with benchstat. On AC: no host 2.669 ms -> 7.188 ms (+169%, p=0.002). Empty host rules 2.874 -> 7.529 ms (+162%). Plus 600 drop entries (1 in 5 file_pointer) 4.223 -> 12.418 ms (+194%). allocs/op 8.086k -> 24.845k. B/op +64%. On battery under heavy co-load: norules 2.885 -> 10.188 ms (+253%) and drops600 9.773 -> 40.344 ms (+313%). pprof (HEAD, no host): holdRoot -> regexp FindAllStringIndex is 0.39 s of 1.13 s in Build (35%); selectorValues is 11%. With 600 drops, gateDropReasons -> reasonWithheld is 0.96 s of 2.80 s (28%). The 600-drop variant is realistic: every non-ephemeral tool use becomes a tool pointer (writer.go:918 upsertToolPointerLocked, no cap), and Truncate emits one tool_pointer drop per pointer it cuts (truncate.go:200-217). Prototypes through -overlay: memoizing holdRoot per text cut the time 20.7% / 33.2% (p<=0.015). Adding a lowercase root-tail prefilter on top cut it 26.0% / 31.7%.

findings.location: internal/rehydrate/pathgate.go:2608-2615 (reasonWithheld field loop); source reason at internal/checkpoint/finalize.go:216
findings.issue: The drop-reason screen reads a leading-slash single-segment token as an absolute POSIX path outside the project, so a slash command embedded in a checkpointer reason is misread as an out-of-project path and the clause is redacted to '(path withheld)'. The finalize pin-reread-failure drop ('invariants'/pins) ends with 'run /qompack:pin --list: <err>'; the token '/qompack:pin' is absLike (leading '/') and inside()=false, so reasonWithheld fires and redactReason replaces the whole clause, hiding the genuine recovery instruction and the underlying error. Summaries already guard this exact shape with driveLessPath() (a single POSIX segment like /review is treated as not-a-path), but reasonWithheld uses plain absLike+inside with no such guard. Over-withholding on a degraded path, not a leak.
findings.evidence: Overlay probe: reasonWithheld("pins could not be re-read at the seal, …; run /qompack:pin --list: pins: store closed")=true; redactReason → "…may be missing; (path withheld): pins: store closed" (both with and without host rules). Same mechanism will redact any reason containing a /qompack:… command or other single-segment /name token.
findings.fix: In reasonWithheld's whitespace-token loop, exclude a driveLess single-segment POSIX token the way summaries do (reuse driveLessPath, or require hasSecondSegment before treating a '/'-led token as an outside absolute path), so '/qompack:pin' and similar slash-command tokens are not read as out-of-project paths. Keep multi-segment '/a/b' and real absolute paths withheld. Add a row to drops_test.go / the reason test asserting the pins-reread reason keeps its 'run /qompack:pin --list' guidance.

findings.issue: Usefulness gap in a common Claude Code shape. Any `name:value` at a path start reads as a PowerShell drive, so ToolSearch's own `select:` previews are withheld in every project, including projects with no deny rules. Claude Code issues those calls to load deferred MCP tools, Qompack's own among them. The live UAT-05 capture shows `{"max_results":1,"query":"select:mcp__plugin_qompack_qompack__record_eliminated"}`. The same rule withholds docker image tags, npm script names, port maps, git revision paths and pytest node ids. ADR 0011 §23 lists most of these as deliberate limits but does not name ToolSearch's `select:`. inertPrefixes already accepts that a user-defined PowerShell drive named `path` or `sha256` is out of scope.
findings.evidence: Overlay reason tracer TestZZReasons at HEAD (in-package pathJudge over the real hostperm RuleSet), run in both a no-rule project and a UAT-style deny project. Withheld, each with reason tokenOutside: `{"max_results":1,"query":"select:mcp__plugin_qompack_qompack__record_eliminated"}`, `{"max_results":3,"query":"select:Read,Edit,Grep"}`, `{"skill":"superpowers:brainstorming"}`, `/qompack:status`, `docker build -t myapp:latest .`, `docker run --rm -it node:20-alpine sh`, `npm run test:unit`, `kubectl port-forward svc/api 8080:80 -n staging`, `git show HEAD:internal/config/load.go`, `pytest tests/test_api.py::TestUsers::test_create -x`. All 10 were shown at a357d187 and at e65ada8f.
findings.fix: Smallest complete step: add `select` (ToolSearch's documented selector) to inertPrefixes, with a row and an ADR §23 item 7(b) line. It carries the same accepted user-drive limit as `path`. Broader step, which needs a coordinator ruling: read a `name:` as a drive only for single letters, PowerShell's built-in drives (Alias, Cert, Env, Function, HKCU, HKLM, Temp, Variable, WSMan) and the `::` provider form. User-defined drives would then fall under the limit already accepted for inertPrefixes.

findings.location: internal/rehydrate/pathgate.go:2225-2233 (rootSpellingOf folds case via paths.DefaultFold, which is true on darwin) vs pathgate.go:495-497 (inside() uses filepath.Rel, which is case-sensitive on darwin); same split in rootPrefix (1128-1140) and exactRooted
findings.issue: On macOS the screen gives a case variant of the project root two different verdicts. Free text treats a case-variant spelling of the root as the project, through the (?i) root regex: `cat /Users/u/PROJ/notes.txt` under root /Users/u/proj is SHOWN. The same path as a structured value goes through inside(), whose filepath.Rel on darwin is case-sensitive, so it is WITHHELD. On the default case-insensitive APFS this only over-withholds the structured form. On a case-sensitive APFS volume (an opt-in setting) /Users/u/PROJ is a different directory outside the project, and the free-text verdict then shows an out-of-project path, which breaks D50's rule. No doc states that Qompack assumes a case-insensitive volume on macOS: grep -i 'case-sensitive' docs/*.md docs/adr/0011* finds nothing. Wave 19h's fix for known item (1) is scoped to Windows, but darwin builds the same (?i) regex. On APFS, U+212A and U+212B decompose canonically to K and Å, so there a Unicode fold over-withholds and does not leak. Whatever 19h changes should state its darwin behaviour.
findings.evidence: No macOS tests were ever run on this code (report-19g: 'macOS was covered by vet and golangci-lint only'). I simulated darwin semantics on a scratch copy: internal/rehydrate with path/filepath replaced by a POSIX shim (case-sensitive Rel, '/' separator), runtime.GOOS set to "darwin", DefaultFold true, paths.Key lower-casing. Probe at root /Users/u/proj with uat12Rules: `PROBE darwin withheld=false  cat /Users/u/PROJ/notes.txt`; `withheld=true  /Users/u/PROJ/notes.txt`; `withheld=true  {"file_path":"/Users/u/PROJ/notes.txt"}`; `withheld=false  grep -r foo /Users/u/PROJ`; `withheld=true  cat /users/u/proj/private/deny.txt`.
findings.fix: Pick one model for darwin and use it everywhere. Either make inside(), key() and rehydrateHostPaths' Rel use the same ASCII fold as rootSpellingOf and rootPrefix on darwin (a case-folding Rel when DefaultFold is true), or stop folding the root on darwin. Then record the case-insensitive-volume assumption, and what a case-sensitive APFS volume costs, as a known limit in docs/security.md and ADR 0011 §23. Add a darwin row once hosted macOS runs this package.

nits.location: internal/rehydrate/pathgate.go:390 (note: basename of every withheld path, outside paths included, goes into knownText)
nits.issue: Usefulness cost that ADR §23 item 7 documents as D61 over-withholding. One Read of a file outside the project teaches its basename to the free-text screen, even with no host rules at all. Typical outside files are a module-cache README.md or a stdlib server.go. Every later Bash, Grep or recall summary that names a project file of the same name is then withheld. Reading dependency sources outside the project is routine in Go, Node, Python and Rust work.
nits.evidence: TestZZOutsideLearn on scratch HEAD, with Deps{} (no host rules). The checkpoint holds outside Reads of <base>/home/go/pkg/mod/github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.8.0/README.md and command.go, and <base>/go1.26/src/net/http/server.go; knownText=[readme.md command.go server.go]. These summaries flip from shown to withheld: `git add README.md`, `git diff --stat -- README.md`, `go vet ./cmd/command.go`, `go test ./internal/server/ -run TestServer && git add internal/server/server.go`, Grep `<R>\cmd\server.go func main`, `{"query":"where is README.md updated"}`, relative Read `README.md`. The absolute Read `<R>\README.md` stays shown (screenExact).
nits.fix: If the owner wants the usefulness back: record an outside path only in knownPaths (drop reasons), not in knownText. A free-text name after a persisted `cd` is already outside the claim ('a name relative to a cd cannot be seen'). Otherwise keep the behaviour and add the module-cache example to the user-facing docs.

nits.location: internal/daemon/drain.go:985 (sum := spoolLineSum(raw) on every line read) and :1471 (spoolLineSum uses fnv.New64a)
nits.issue: Wave 20's memo computes a byte-at-a-time FNV-64a sum of every spool line a pass reads. That includes fresh lines that the memo neither holds nor will compare. The sum lives only in memory, so its speed is all that matters.
nits.evidence: Micro-benchmark on this host: FNV-64a runs at 342-408 MB/s. For a 1 MiB line (ipc.MaxLineBytes) it costs 3.07 ms, against 17.5 ms to JSON-decode the same line, so about 18% extra on the largest lines. It is small next to admission, which costs about 13 ms per line by the w20 report.
nits.fix: Compute the sum only when it is needed: when memoLines holds lineStart, or when consume records the line out of order. Alternatively, use hash/maphash with a per-drainer seed, about 10x faster; the sum is never persisted.
